Question: Official name
ROR ID
Why it matters: Lets repositories and funders credit outputs to the institution. Free to request.

Question: Zenodo community
Why it matters: An existing shop window for outputs, at no cost.

Question: Contact for this registry (name, role)
Why it matters: One named person keeps the column current.

Question: Consulted (date, who attended)
Why it matters: Turns a draft column into a confirmed one.

Question: Productivity suite: Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, or both?
Why it matters: Decides which storage, forms and dashboard tools come at no extra cost.

Question: Can people outside the institution get access to files and forms? How?
Why it matters: Decides whether cross-island projects can run in the institution's own tools.

Question: Storage per person and per project; are shared drives available for research?
Why it matters: Personal storage leaves with the person.

Question: Where does research data actually sit during a project today?
Why it matters: The honest answer is the baseline.

Question: Rules for sensitive data (personal, health, student records): where may it be stored?
Why it matters: Rules out some tools before anyone chooses them.

Question: Institutional repository? Platform and URL.
Can the institution mint DOIs? By which route: own DataCite prefix, a consortium, or only through Zenodo, OSF or Dataverse?
Why it matters: Most institutions need no DOI membership of their own.

Question: ORCID: institutional membership? Roughly what share of researchers has one?
Who looks after theses, reports and datasets once they are finished: library, research office, nobody?
Why it matters: Names the person a repository decision would land on.

Question: Any journal or report series that needs DOIs?
Why it matters: Decides whether Crossref is relevant.

Question: Licensed quantitative software: product, number of seats, who may use it, home use?
Licensed qualitative software: product, number of seats, who may use it?
Computer labs: operating system, and can users install R, Python and packages themselves?
Why it matters: Installation is where workshops lose their first morning.

Question: Browser tools enabled on institutional accounts (Google Colab, Posit Cloud)?
Why it matters: The fallback when installation is blocked.

Question: Licence renewal month and budget holder for each paid tool.
Why it matters: A switch can only happen at renewal.

Question: Research data or open science policy: title, year, link?
Support for data management plans: template, reviewer?
A named data steward, librarian or champion for research data?
Does ethics review check data management and consent for data sharing?
Why it matters: Consent decides what can ever be shared.

Question: Data or software training offered in the last 12 months.
Planned changes in the next 12 to 24 months: new licences, cancellations, migrations?
What could the institution share with partners on other islands: licences, servers, trainers?
Why it matters: Where one institution's capacity can serve the network.

Question: What would the institution want from the network?
Is there an AI policy or guidance for staff and students?
Why it matters: Tells people what is allowed before they find out the hard way.

Question: Does the institution hold AI accounts, and under which agreement?
Why it matters: Decides whether data typed into AI tools falls under an institutional contract or under personal terms.

Question: Is the AI chat in the existing Microsoft 365 or Google licence switched on, and for whom?
Why it matters: Often already paid for, and the cheapest protected option.

Question: Which data may go into which AI tools, and who decides?
Why it matters: Personal and confidential data needs a rule, not individual judgement.
